name: Operator Algebras

papers.title: Co-amenability and local reflexivity of $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset B$ be a unital inclusion of $C^*$-algebras. We prove that local reflexivity passes from $A$ to $B$ if the inclusion $A^{**}\subset B^{**}$ is co-amenable. It follows that local reflexivity is preserved by minimal tensor products with exact $C^*$-algebras, by inductive limits over directed sets, and by reduced crossed products by discrete amenable groups. We also prove that reduced free products with respect to states with faithful GNS representations preserve local reflexivity and that every locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra embeds into a simple locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra. These results answer Questions~(b), (c), (d), (f) and~(h) in Kirchberg's 2011 list.

papers.title: On Shepp's property in free probability
papers.abstract: We establish a free analogue of Shepp's theorem for freely independent standard semicircular elements. We show more generally that a family of self-normalized squared quadratic forms is free, and each has a standard Marchenko-Pastur distribution. The free analogue of Shepp's theorem follows by taking the coefficients of quadratic forms to be the three Pauli matrices. We also prove some new free analogues of Lukacs-type independence results. The key part of the proof is a construction of an equivalent and simpler operator model on a corner algebra compressed by a free projection.

papers.title: Duality of finite-dimensional Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra actions via inclusions
papers.abstract: We study actions of finite-dimensional Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras on a unital $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra $A$. We first define the Rokhlin property and approximate representability directly for an action $H\curvearrowright A$ and characterize these properties, under appropriate hypotheses, in terms of the corresponding properties of the canonical conditional expectation $E\colon A\to A^H$. Based on this characterization, we establish the following duality for a saturated action on a simple unital $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra $A$ such that $A\rtimes H$ is simple: 1. $H\curvearrowright A$ has the Rokhlin property if and only if the dual action $H^{\circ}\curvearrowright A\rtimes H$ is approximately representable. 2. $H\curvearrowright A$ is approximately representable if and only if the dual action $H^{\circ}\curvearrowright A\rtimes H$ has the Rokhlin property. For separable $A$, we also identify these properties with the corresponding spatial formulations introduced by Barlak--Szab{\'o}--Voigt, assuming saturation in the Rokhlin comparison. We present examples of Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra actions both with and without the Rokhlin property.

papers.title: Ultrarank and ideal structure of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ideal structure of the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ for a coarse disjoint union $X = \bigsqcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} X_n$ of finite metric spaces, with a focus on ideals lying between the compact ideal $\mathcal{K}$ and the ghost ideal $\mathcal{G}$. To analyze these ideals, we introduce a nonstandard invariant called the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank of an operator, which is stable under compact perturbations and completely characterizes principal ideal inclusions in the block-diagonal Calkin algebra. Using the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank as an obstruction to ideal inclusion in $C^*_u(X)$, we construct an ideal between $\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ that cannot be written as the intersection of any geometric ideal and the ghost ideal. On the positive side, when the averaging projection $P$ belongs to $C^*_u(X)$, we prove that the closed two-sided ideal $\langle P \rangle$ generated by $P$ equals $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if every ghost operator has finite ultrarank and $X$ has zero-density Property A, and we classify all closed two-sided ideals of $C^*_u(X)$ in this case.

papers.title: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
papers.abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.

papers.title: Linearization of completely Lipschitz functions
papers.abstract: We develop a linearization theory for completely Lipschitz mappings between operator spaces. Motivated by the classical theory of Lipschitz-free spaces, we introduce a completely Lipschitz-free space and show that completely Lipschitz mappings admit a canonical linearization as completely bounded operators on this space. We provide several equivalent descriptions of this operator space, extending to the noncommutative setting the classical constructions of Arens--Eells, de Leeuw, and Dixmier--Ng. In particular, we obtain a molecular description, a quotient representation of an operator $\ell_1$-space, and a realization as the closed linear span of evaluation functionals. Our framework applies over both the real and complex scalar fields; in the real case, we first establish some operator space results needed to carry out the constructions. We also show that our notion of completely Lipschitz mapping encompasses the previously introduced extensions of Lipschitz mappings to operator spaces. These results provide a unified framework for studying Lipschitz phenomena in the setting of operator spaces and establish the corresponding free operator spaces as a natural tool for their linearization.
